current.text: He is new in Philadelphia this season and is set to be the sixth man.
Projected starting five: Maxey, Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James and Embiid. Simons comes off the bench behind them.
Last season his rim finishing jumped from 58 to 70 percent (88th percentile). Before that he was in the lower half of the league.
As a backup in Philadelphia, his numbers should come down, and his rim finishing is not expected to hold.
Philadelphia's usage is crowded with Maxey, Embiid, LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. That leaves few shots for a bench guard.
Nick Nurse plays his starters, guards in particular, very heavy minutes. That caps the minutes left for a sixth man.
New arrivals, Simons among them, are expected to cut into Maxey's minutes.
Yahoo lists him as questionable with an undisclosed issue.
The 76ers have 13 back-to-backs, and three of them fall in the fantasy playoffs.
He is not a draft target in a 144-player league. He is worth watching on waivers when Embiid misses games or LeBron James sits.

durable.text: He is a shooter. His value comes from threes and a high FT% on low volume, and he gives little in rebounds, steals and blocks.

note: Yahoo ranks him 201 and ESPN ranks him 222, with both sites at 0 USD. Do not repeat the 7 USD our league paid last season: as the sixth man behind four high-usage stars under a coach who rides his starters, he is outside the 144 players worth drafting. His threes (2.5 per game) and 90% FT% can help a 3PM build off waivers, but 43% on about 12 shots, low steals and three playoff back-to-backs limit him. Early on, check his Q status, his bench minutes and whether he gets more of them when Embiid or LeBron James sit.
